Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision-making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision-making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!

Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 24. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Article 72

1. Prevention of VAC involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 70 letter a shall be implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
2. Standards for the prevention of VAC involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Procedures for the prevention of VAC involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of:a. development and strengthening of institutional VAC prevention;
b. policy advocacy and assistance or technical guidance on the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the prevention of VAC in the Regency Area; andc. coordination and synchronization of VAC prevention in the Regency Area.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

Part Seven Implementation

Paragraph 1 Scope

Article 37

The implementation of Protection of Women in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 21 paragraph (1), consists of:
a. prevention of VAW involving parties in the Regency Area;
b. provision of services for women victims of Violence requiring coordination in the Regency Area; andc. strengthening and development of Women's Protection Service Provider Institutions in the Regency Area.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision-making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision-making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that has an impact on, or has an impact similar to physical, psychological, and sexual or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment and alternative care rights, basic health and welfare rights, as well as education rights, leisure time utilization, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER VII COOPERATION

Article 96

1. In order to support the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Administration in the Regency Area, the Regency Regional Government may conduct Regional cooperation.
2. Regional cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted by the Regency Regional Government with:a. other regions;
b. third parties; and/orc. institutions or regional governments abroad.
3. Regional cooperation with institutions or regional governments abroad as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c, is conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. Regional cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is set forth in a cooperation agreement.
5. Regional cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented by referring to laws and regulations governing regional cooperation.

CHAPTER IX COORDINATION

Article 98

1. The Regent conducts coordination in the administration of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Regency Area with the Governor and/or relevant Ministries.
2. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:a. planning;
b. implementation;
c. monitoring; andd. evaluation.
3. Coordination as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 53

The Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the Regency as referred to in Article 52, consists of:
a. institutionalization of the Fulfillment of Children's Rights in government, non-government, and Business World institutions in the Regency; andb. strengthening and development of Service Provider Institutions for Improving the Quality of Children's Lives in the Regency.

Article 75

1. Provision of services for CNSP requiring coordination in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 70 letter b shall be implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
2. Standards for the provision of services for CNSP as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be the standards for Child Protection services.
3. Procedures for the provision of services for CNSP as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of:a. provision of community complaint services for CNSP in the Regency Area including:
1. establishment of UPTD PPA in the Regency Area;
2. implementation of UPTD PPA services; and
3. provision and strengthening of service provider human resources through training and certification of CNSP protection services.  b. coordination and synchronization of the implementation of CNSP assistance in the Regency Area including:
1. coordination …
1. cross-Regional Apparatus coordination for the implementation of CNSP service provision;
2. policy development and implementation of an integrated CNSP handling system across related Regional Apparatus;
3. guidance to the Regency Area in handling CNSP; and
4. data collection, monitoring, and evaluation of CNSP case services.

Article 78

1. Strengthening and development of Service Provider Institutions for CNSP in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 70 letter c shall be implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
2. Standards for strengthening and development of service provider institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include standards for child-friendly Special Protection institutions.
3. Procedures for strengthening and development of CNSP service provider institutions in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:a. coordination and synchronization of the provision of service facilities and infrastructure for CNSP in the Regency Area;
b. capacity building …b. capacity building of human resources of Service Provider Institutions for CNSP in the Regency Area; andc. strengthening networks among Service Provider Institutions for CNSP in the Regency Area.

Article 39

1. Prevention of KTP involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 37 letter a, is implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
2. Standards for KTP prevention as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. institutional implementers of KTP prevention in the Regency Area;
b. understanding of KTP; andc. integration of KTP prevention policies across all development sectors.
3. Procedures for KTP prevention as referred to in paragraph (1) include:a. coordination and synchronization of implementation of policies, programs, and KTP prevention activities in the Regency Area, consisting of:

3. building cooperation on KTP prevention involving parties in the Regency Area.  b. policy advocacy and service assistance for Women's Protection in the Regency Area, covering:
1. building commitment in KTP prevention;
2. integrating KTP prevention into Regency regional development planning; and
3. encouraging increased Community Participation and cooperation with the Business World and mass media in KTP prevention.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree. 33. CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision-making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision-making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that has an impact on, or has an impact similar to physical, psychological, and sexual or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment and alternative care rights, basic health and welfare rights, as well as education rights, leisure time utilization, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 39. I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. 16. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Article 62 Paragraph (1)

Point a "Children in Emergency Situations" means Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point b "Children in Conflict with the Law" means Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts.

Point c "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" means Children who are left behind, at the forefront, at the outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.

Point d "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" means Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.

"Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" means Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and sexual abuse.

Point e "Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" means Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.

Point f "Children Who Are Victims of Pornography" means Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.

Point g "Children with HIV and AIDS" means Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.

Point h "Child Victims of Kidnapping" means Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.

"Child Victims of Sale" means Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to another party for compensation or other reasons.

"Child Victims of Trafficking" means Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.

Point i "Child Victims of Physical Violence" means Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.

"Child Victims of Psychological Violence" means Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.

Point j "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" means Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point k "Child Victims of Terrorism Networks" means Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by acts of terrorism either as child victims, child perpetrators, children of perpetrators, and child witnesses.

Point 1 "Children with Disabilities" means Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.

Point m "Child Victims of Maltreatment" means Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not met properly either physically, spiritually, or socially.

Point n "Child Victims of Maltreatment" means Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not met properly either physically, spiritually, or socially.

"Child Victims of Neglect" means Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.

Point o "Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Their Parents' Condition" means Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a stigma or bad view from labeling related to their parents' condition.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

Point j "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" means Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

"Child Victims of Neglect" means Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision-making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision-making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that has an impact on, or has an impact similar to physical, psychological, and sexual or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Point a "Children in Emergency Situations" means Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point d "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" means Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.

Point g "Children with HIV and AIDS" means Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.

Point h "Child Victims of Kidnapping" means Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.

"Child Victims of Trafficking" means Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision-making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision-making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that has an impact on, or has an impact similar to physical, psychological, and sexual or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment and alternative care rights, basic health and welfare rights, as well as education rights, leisure time utilization, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision-making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision-making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that has an impact on, or has an impact similar to physical, psychological, and sexual or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment and alternative care rights, basic health and welfare rights, as well as education rights, leisure time utilization, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37.
