Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, resulting from the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 43. Business World is micro enterprises, small enterprises, medium enterprises, and large enterprises that carry out economic activities in Indonesia and are domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45. Community Participation is the participation of community members to channel their aspirations, thoughts, and interests in the administration of Regional Government. 46. Community Organization hereinafter referred to as Ormas is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities, and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 47. Social Conflict hereinafter referred to as Conflict is a feud and/or physical clash with Violence between two or more community groups that lasts for a certain time and has a broad impact resulting in insecurity and social disintegration thereby disrupting national stability and hindering national development. 48.

Point a "Children in Emergency Situations" means Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disrupts the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point 1 "Children with Disabilities" means Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.

Part One Definitions

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean: 1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision-making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision-making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by gender-based roles and labeling, which denies human dignity and the right to self that has an impact on, or has an impact similar to physical, psychological, and sexual or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 24. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment and alternative care rights, basic health and welfare rights, as well as education rights, leisure time utilization, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Children in Need of Special Protection hereinafter abbreviated as AMPK are Children in emergency situations, Children in conflict with the law, Children from minority and isolated groups, Children who are economically and/or sexually exploited, Children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse, Children who are victims of pornography, Children with HIV/AIDS, Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, and/or trafficking, Children who are victims of physical and/or psychological violence, Children who are victims of sexual crimes, Children who are victims of terrorism networks, Children with disabilities, Children who are victims of abuse and neglect, Children with deviant social behavior, and Children who are victims of stigmatization from labeling related to their parents' condition, and Children with other problems. 30. Gender Data is data regarding the relationship of relations in status, roles, and conditions between men and women. 31. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of Gender and Child Data consisting of components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/institutions and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of the results of policies/programs/activities of Gender Responsive and Child-sensitive development. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree. 33. Family Quality is the condition of the Family determined by the dimensions of quality of legality and structure, quality of physical resilience, quality of economic resilience, quality of socio-psychological resilience, and quality of socio-cultural resilience in realizing Gender Equality and Child Rights. 34. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 35. Violence Against Women hereinafter abbreviated as KTP is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 36. Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the scope of the household. 38. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, resulting from the criminal act of trafficking in persons. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 43. Business World is micro enterprises, small enterprises, medium enterprises, and large enterprises that carry out economic activities in Indonesia and are domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45. Community Participation is the participation of community members to channel their aspirations, thoughts, and interests in the administration of Regional Government. 46. Community Organization hereinafter referred to as Ormas is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities, and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 47. Social Conflict hereinafter referred to as Conflict is a feud and/or physical clash with Violence between two or more community groups that lasts for a certain time and has a broad impact resulting in insecurity and social disintegration thereby disrupting national stability and hindering national development. 48.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

Part Seven Child-Friendly Regency

Article 81

1. The Regency Regional Government shall implement CFC in the Regency Area.
2. Implementation of CFC in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through the integration of policies, programs, and activities for the development of the Central Government and the Regency Regional Government.
3. Further provisions regarding the Implementation of CFC as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a separate Regional Regulation.

Article 100

1. The Regency Regional Government may establish an evaluation Team in conducting evaluation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection administration.
2. The establishment of the evaluation team as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent Decree.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted annually.
3. The results of the evaluation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection become input material in the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the coming year.
4. Further provisions regarding monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection administration in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1), are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER V IMPROVEMENT OF FAMILY QUALITY

Part One General

Article 82 (1) The Regency Regional Government shall have the authority to implement the Improvement of Family Quality in the Regency Area.

3. Implementation of the Improvement of Family Quality in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Regional Apparatus implementing governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and implementing the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improving family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, continuous, and sustainable manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and establish by Regional Regulation.
